P.J. Les Termes de Référence 

DIRECTION GENERALE DU TRESOR ET DE LA COMPTABILITE PUBLIQUE (DGTCP)

TERMES DE RÉFÉRENCE (TDR)

Recrutement d’un Expert chargé d'établir les principes et méthodes d’inventaire et d’accompagner la DGTCP dans leur mise en œuvre

Contexte et justification

Le Ministère de l’Économie et des Finances (MEF), à travers la Direction Générale du Trésor et de la Comptabilité Publique (DGTCP), s’est engagé dans un processus de modernisation des finances publiques visant le passage d’un système de comptabilité de caisse modifiée à un système de comptabilité en droits constatés.

Cette transition implique la mise en place de nouveaux référentiels, dont le Plan Comptable de l’État Haïtien (PCEH), et nécessite l’établissement d’un bilan d’ouverture fiable, reposant entre autres sur l’identification, la valorisation et l’enregistrement du patrimoine de l’État.

Dans cette perspective, l’État doit se doter de principes, normes, procédures et méthodes uniformes d’inventaire couvrant l’ensemble des actifs, passifs, biens meubles et immeubles, stocks, immobilisations, créances et dettes.

La DGTCP souhaite donc recruter, dans le cadre du Projet de Renforcement de la Gestion des Finances Publiques (PREGEFIP), un expert spécialisé en inventaire patrimonial et en comptabilité publique capable d’élaborer ces outils méthodologiques et d’appuyer leur mise en œuvre opérationnelle.

Objectif général

Développer un cadre méthodologique complet et opérationnel d’inventaire des actifs et passifs à long terme de l’État haïtien, et accompagner la DGTCP dans la conduite des travaux d’inventaire, en vue de compléter ou de réviser la stratégie du bilan d’ouverture qui sera élaborée par l’OCPAH dans le cadre du passage de la comptabilité de caisse à la comptabilité en droits constatés.

Objectifs spécifiques

L’expert devra:

  1. Établir les principes directeurs, normes et standards d’inventaire conformément aux exigences de la comptabilité en droits constatés.
  2. Développer des procédures et méthodes d’inventaire applicables à l’ensemble des entités publiques.
  3. Élaborer des outils opérationnels : fiches d’inventaire, registres, formulaires, guides pratiques, canevas de rapports.
  4. Définir une méthodologie de valorisation des actifs et passifs, y compris en cas d’absence de données fiables.
  5. Contribuer à l’élaboration d’une stratégie nationale d’inventaire, incluant la planification, la coordination institutionnelle et la gestion logistique.
  6. Appuyer la DGTCP dans la conduite pilote d’opérations d’inventaire dans un échantillon d’administrations.
  7. Former les équipes techniques de la DGTCP et des entités pilotes sur les principes et méthodes retenus.
  8. Accompagner la consolidation des résultats et formuler des recommandations pour l’extension nationale de la démarche.

Résultats attendus

À l’issue de la mission, les livrables suivants sont attendus :

  1. Un cadre normatif d’inventaire comprenant :
  • principes directeurs ;
  • définitions ;
  • classification des actifs et passifs ;
  • normes d’évaluation et de valorisation.
  1. Un manuel méthodologique d’inventaire incluant :
  • procédures détaillées ;
  • rôles et responsabilités ;
  • mécanismes de contrôle interne ;
  • modalités de documentation des opérations.
  1. Des outils techniques opérationnels : formulaires, registres, canevas d’état des lieux, fiches de saisie.
  2. Une stratégie de mise en œuvre au niveau national, incluant un calendrier et un dispositif institutionnel.
  3. Un rapport d’accompagnement technique sur les inventaires pilotes réalisés.
  4. Un module de formation et les supports pédagogiques correspondants.

 

 

Tâches et responsabilités de l’expert

L’expert devra :

  • Analyser les référentiels existants (PCEH, normes internationales pertinentes, documents MEF, ORMH et Autres).
  • Diagnostiquer les pratiques actuelles d’inventaire dans les entités publiques.
  • Proposer une approche harmonisée répondant aux exigences comptables.
  • Élaborer les outils et procédures d’inventaire.
  • Organiser et animer des ateliers techniques avec la DGTCP.
  • Accompagner des missions d’inventaire sur terrain.
  • Appuyer la consolidation et l’évaluation des inventaires pilotes.
  • Produire l’ensemble des documents attendus et en assurer la validation technique.

Profil recherché

L’expert devra présenter les qualifications suivantes :

Compétences académiques :

  • Diplôme universitaire (Master ou équivalent) en comptabilité publique, gestion financière, audit, gestion patrimoniale ou domaine connexe.

Expérience professionnelle :

  • Minimum 7 ans d’expérience dans les inventaires d’actifs, la gestion patrimoniale ou la comptabilité publique.
  • Expérience avérée dans l’élaboration de référentiels méthodologiques d’inventaire ou d’évaluations patrimoniales.
  • Expérience dans les réformes de finances publiques, idéalement dans le passage de la comptabilité de caisse à la comptabilité en droits constatés.
  • Connaissance des normes IPSAS : un atout majeur.
  • Expérience en renforcement de capacités et conduite de formations.
  • Expérience de travail dans le secteur public : fortement souhaitée.

Compétences spécifiques :

  • Capacité d’analyse et de rédaction technique.
  • Maîtrise des méthodologies d’inventaire physique et comptable.
  • Sens de la pédagogie et du transfert de compétences

Durée et modalités de la mission

La durée prévue de la mission est de cinq (5) mois, incluant :

  • élaboration du cadre méthodologique ;
  • appui opérationnel aux inventaires pilotes ;
  • formation et transfert de compétences ;
  • consolidation des rapports.

Interlocuteurs principaux

  1. Directeur Général Adjoint chargé de la gestion du Trésor
  2. Comité Sectoriel de Suivi des Réformes du Trésor (COSRET)
  3. Commission de Réforme des Finances Publiques et de la Gouvernance Economique (CRFP/GE)
  4. Coordination des Postes Comptables et de la Normalisation Comptable (CPCNC)
  5. Direction des Comptes Publics
  6. Responsable projet PAGEFIS ou Comité SIGFIP
  7. Directeurs Techniques et Chefs de Service de la DGTCP
  8. les entités administratives sélectionnées pour les inventaires pilotes.

Modalités de supervision

L’expert sera placé sous la supervision directe du Directeur Général du Trésor et de la Comptabilité Publique.
Le Comité sectoriel de suivi des reformes (COSRET) de la DGTCP assurera le suivi des livrables et des validations intermédiaires.

Conditions de travail

La DGTCP mettra à la disposition de l’expert :

  • les documents et données nécessaires ;
  • les facilités logistiques pour les missions de terrain ;
  • les facilités d’accès aux entités pilotes.

  • Maîtrise des méthodologies d’inventaire physique et comptable.
  • Sens de la pédagogie et du transfert de compétences

Durée et modalités de la mission

La durée prévue de la mission est de cinq (5) mois, incluant :

  • élaboration du cadre méthodologique ;
  • appui opérationnel aux inventaires pilotes ;
  • formation et transfert de compétences ;
  • consolidation des rapports.

Interlocuteurs principaux

  1. Directeur Général Adjoint chargé de la gestion du Trésor
  2. Comité Sectoriel de Suivi des Réformes du Trésor (COSRET)
  3. Commission de Réforme des Finances Publiques et de la Gouvernance Economique (CRFP/GE)
  4. Coordination des Postes Comptables et de la Normalisation Comptable (CPCNC)
  5. Direction des Comptes Publics
  6. Responsable projet PAGEFIS ou Comité SIGFIP
  7. Directeurs Techniques et Chefs de Service de la DGTCP
  8. les entités administratives sélectionnées pour les inventaires pilotes.

Modalités de supervision

L’expert sera placé sous la supervision directe du Directeur Général du Trésor et de la Comptabilité Publique.
Le Comité sectoriel de suivi des reformes (COSRET) de la DGTCP assurera le suivi des livrables et des validations intermédiaires.

Conditions de travail

La DGTCP mettra à la disposition de l’expert :

Invitation for Proposals

(Consulting Services) 

 

UKRAINE

 

Project: Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine (LEARN) Project

 

Grant no.: TF0C5794

 

Name of the Contract: Audit of UIED

 

Contract number: LEARN-2.1-UIED-AUDIT

Market Approach - Open, National

Ukraine received the URTF Grant No. TF0C5794 from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) in US dollars to finance the Ukraine Improving Higher Education for Results Project and intends to use part of the funds to make payments under the Contract No. LEARN-2.1-UIED-AUDIT "Audit of UIED" .

 

The Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine invites eligible participants (Consultant; Participant) to submit sealed proposals for the provision of the following services: audit and development of the institutional strategy and implementation plan of the state institution "Ukrainian Institute for Education Development" (“Services”). Detailed information about the Services is provided in the Terms of Reference (Section 7) of the Request for Proposals.

 

The selection of Consultant will be carried out through Quality and Cost-based Selection (QCBS) based on a simplified technical proposal as specified in the Request for Proposals, in accordance with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, as revised in September 2025, available at the link www.worldbank.org 


 

The expected duration of the provision of services is 5 (five) months from the date of signing the contract.

 

IBRD requires compliance with the Bank's Anti-Corruption Guidelines and its applicable sanctions policies and procedures, as outlined in the World Bank Group Sanctions Framework. In further compliance with this policy, Bidders shall permit and require their agents (whether declared or not), subcontractors, sub-consultants, service providers, suppliers and personnel to permit the Bank to inspect all invoices, records and other documents relating to the request for quotations and execution of the contract (in case of award), as well as for their verification by auditors appointed by the Bank.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

The technical proposals of the consultants will be evaluated in two parts. The following are the mandatory criteria that the consultants must meet. Technical proposals of consultants that do not meet the criteria listed below will not be evaluated and the proposal will be rejected:

 

  • The Consultant shall be a reputable consulting firm/group of consultants with proven knowledge and have at least five (5) years of proven experience in institutional development and/or organizational audit.
  • At least two similar tasks in the last 5 years (to be confirmed by copies of contracts, acts of work performed/services rendered, letters of recommendation).
  • Average annual turnover for the last two (2) years is not less than 50,000 USD.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

Interested eligible participants can receive additional information, a complete set of the Request for Proposals, including the terms of reference, the proposal submission form and the contract form, as well as information on terms of submission of proposals upon request by email oleksandr.radchenko@uiherp.org (Subject: LEARN-2.1-UIED-AUDIT Request for Proposals) or using the following link:

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

(Consulting Services – Firms Selection)

Country:                           Independent State of Samoa

Name of Project:              Digitally Connected and Resilient Samoa Project (DCSRP)  

Grant No.:                         E379-WS

Assignment title:              Development of Critical Information Infrastructure Protection (CIIP) Capacities

Reference No.:                  DSP/CS/03

1. The Government of Samoa (GoS) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the DCRSP P180807 and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. This project aims to enhance the capacity of the Government to deliver digitally enabled, inclusive, secure and safe public services. The Project will focus on digital connectivity and digital government infrastructure, including an upgrade and extension of Samoa’s national fiber network, alongside measures to enhance cybersecurity resilience and safeguard the reliability of essential digital services.

2. The Consulting services (“Services”) will support the design, establishment and operationalization of Samoa’s Critical Information Infrastructure Protection (CIIP) framework. This will include the development of governance, legal and institutional frameworks; the identification of critical information infrastructures (CIIs) across government sectors and the preparation of practical guidelines to assist the CII operators in protecting and managing critical systems and assets. The Services will also support the implementation of the CIIP framework by establishing effective coordination, supervision and oversight mechanisms while strengthening national capacity through technical guidance and stakeholder engagement. The assignment will be executed by the selected firm, with an estimated duration of 24 months, ensuring the completion of all tasks within the specified timeline. The consulting firm is expected to commence work in May 2026.

3. The Ministry of Communications and Information Technology now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:  

  1. At least five (5) years of experience in conducting Cybersecurity or ICT Security matters on a national level. Demonstrated experience working with government and public sector institutions, particularly in areas related to critical information infrastructure, will be considered an advantage
    • Experience in CIIP planning and frameworks, Critical Infrastructure (CI) Identification Procedures; Guideline development and implementation; and experience in CERT operations or cyber exercises
  2. Demonstrated expertise in risk assessment, incident response and CII governance
  3. Experience facilitating technical workshops, consultations or capacity building sessions with government agencies, regulators and operators.
  4. Strong background in capacity building and training, with experience in designing and delivering training programs.
  5. Moderate experience in and / or demonstrates a proficiency level enough to lead the planning, development and execution of a stakeholder strategy in support of the defined objectives.
    • Stakeholder Strategy, Planning and Execution

4. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14,3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2023, setting forth the World Bank’s Policy on conflict of interest.

5. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture (“JV”) and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a JV, all the partners in the JV shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. 

6. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations in paragraph 4. 

7. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following websites: Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (www.mcit.gov.ws) and the Ministry of Finance  (www.mof.gov.ws/tender-adverisements)

8. Further information can be obtained at the address below during working hours from 9.00am to 4.00pm, Samoa time, on working days:

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

For Monitoring & Evaluation Consultancy Services (Firms Selection)

Package Number: BSTRONG/LGED/S-02

 

  1. The People’s Republic of Bangladesh has received a credit from the International Development Association (IDA) towards the cost of the Bangladesh Sustainable Recovery, Emergency Preparedness and Response Project (B-STRONG). LGED, an implementing agency of the Project intends to apply a part of the proceeds of this credit to eligible payments under the contract for which this Request for Expression of Interest is invited.
  2. The broad scope of consulting services (“the Services”) includes developing standardized tools, strengthening data collection and reporting, and ensuring data quality and consistency across agencies. The Consultant will also build institutional capacity and provide regular analytical feedback to support evidence-based decision-making. Overall, the services will enable timely monitoring of progress, outcomes, and key implementation risks.
  3. The main objectives of the consulting services is to engage the services of an experienced consulting firm to support LGED in establishing and operationalizing a harmonized M&E system and in consolidating and reporting Results Framework indicators for Components 1, 2 and 5 (LGED, BWDB and SDF) of the Bangladesh Sustainable Recovery, Emergency Preparedness and Response Project (B-STRONG).The Consultant will provide regular feedback to the Project Director (PD), LGED/PMU and participating agencies, and support evidence-based decision making through timely and accurate monitoring of project inputs, outputs, outcomes and key implementation risks.
  4. The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) can be found at the following website: www.lged.gov.bd. The ToR or any further information can be obtained at the address of the undersigned given below, during office hours from 9:00 am to 5:00 pm Bangladesh Standard Time (BST).
  5. The Local Government Engineering Department (LGED) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services.  The shortlisting criteria are:
  1. General Experience of the Firm in providing services (core business and years in business);
  2. Experience in similar assignments of compatible size, complexity and technical specialty in the required areas;
  3. Experience in similar assignments in development partners funded Projects.
  4. Overall staffing and logistics of the firm.

 

Key experts will not be evaluated at shortlisting stage.

 

Consultants are requested to submit, but not limited to, the following supporting documents in support of the above-mentioned criteria:

(i) The Firm's Incorporation/Trade/registration documents from the country of the firm (ii) Firm’s brochures; (iii) description of similar consultancy contracts, including the scope, contract amount (Additionally Specifying amount of the assignment involvement of the Firm), Man months, name of Client, period of the contract (date of contract signing to date of completion), location/ country of the services, etc.

 

  1. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Sixth Edition, February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.
  2. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but shall indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture (i.e. all members of the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable) and/or a sub-consultancy (i.e. the Consultant will be responsible, including for the services of the sub-consultant). In case of an association, the Consultant must explain in the EoI submission (a) the rationale/ justification for the proposed inclusion of the JV members and/or sub-consultants; and (b) the anticipated role and relevant qualifications of each member of the Joint Venture and/or of each sub-consultant for carrying out the assignment. Failure to provide the above explanation in the EoI may risk the association not being shortlisted for the assignment. However, the qualifications/ experience of sub-consultants will not be considered by the Client in the evaluation of Expressions of Interest for Shortlisting purposes.
  3. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method as set forth in the World Bank Procurement Regulations.  
  4. The duration of the consultancy services is tentatively 36 months. Probable start date of the Service is 1st October 2026.
  5. Expression of Interest needs to be submitted (either through e-mail or in person or by mail) to the Project Director’s Office (Workshop Bhaban, Level-3, LGED HQ) by 15:00 local time (GMT+6:00 hours) on April 23, 2026. Please clearly mention “Expression of Interest (EoI) for Selection of Monitoring & Evaluation Consultancy Service (Firm) under B-STRONG (LGED)” in the e-mail’s subject line or on the top of the envelope.
  6. The authority reserves the right to accept or reject any or all EOIs.

الجهة المشترية : وزارة المالية والتخطيط دولة فلسطين              

اسم المناقصة : توريد أجهزة ومعدات تكنولوجيا المعلومات لصالح عدة وزارات -ICT Equipment

رقم المناقصة : GZ-MOPIC-512328-GO-RFQ/ GZ-MOPIC-508461-GO-RFQ

  1. تود  وزارة المالية والتخطيط استخدام جزء من مخصصاتها ضمن مشروع التعافي الإجتماعي وخلق فرص عمل والممول من قبل البنك الدولي لتسديد المبالغ المستحقة بموجب عقد توريد أجهزة ومعدات تكنولوجيا المعلومات لصالح عدة وزارات حكومية -ICT Equipment، مناقصة رقم: GZ-MOPIC-512328-GO-RFQ/ GZ-MOPIC-508461-GO-RFQ
  2. تدعو  وزارة المالية والتخطيط المناقصين ذوي الأهلية الى تقديم عطاءات بالظرف المختوم توريد أجهزة ومعدات تكنولوجيا المعلومات لصالح عدة وزارات حكومية  -  ICT Equipment من خلال مشروع التعافي الإجتماعي وخلق فرص عمل، مناقصة و يحق للمناقص التقدم لواحدة أو أكثر من البنود.
  3. ستتم المناقصة العامة من خلال طلب عطاءات تنافسية محلية وفقا لمقتضيات قانون الشراء العام رقم 8 لعام 2014 ولائحته التنفيذية، وهي مفتوحة لكل المناقصين ذوي الأهلية، والمؤهلات المطلوب توفرها لدى المناقص الفائز هي: توفر الخبرات السابقة في نفس المجال (توريد أجهزة ومعدات تكنولوجيا المعلومات بمواصفات وجودة عالية، وتوفر الملاءة المالية.
  4. يمكن للمناقصين المؤهلين والمهتمين الحصول على معلومات إضافية من وحدة مشروع التعافي الإجتماعي وخلق فرص عمل الممول من البنك الدولي في وزارة المالية والتخطيط وكذلك فحص وثائق المناقصة على العنوان المبين أدناه وذلك من الساعة الثامنة صباحاً إلى الساعة الثالثة بعد الظهر من أيام الأحد الى الخميس، أو عبر خلال البوابة الموحدة للشراء العام shiraa.gov.ps. على أن يتم مراعاة إدخال بريد إلكتروني معتمد خاص بالمناقص لتزويده بأي تعديلات تطرأ على الوثائق، أو من خلال زيارة وحدة مشروع البنك الدولي في وزارة المالية والتخطيط على العنوان المبين أدناه وذلك من الساعة 9:00 صباحاً إلى الساعة 2:00 مساءً من أيام الأحد إلى الخميس.
  5. يجب تسليم العطاءات في العنوان المبين أسفل الدعوة قبل يوم الأربعاء الموافق 29/4/2026 الساعة 12:00 ظهراً، والعطاءات الإلكترونية غير مقبولة، ويجب أن تكون صلاحية العطاءات سارية لمدة 120يوما بعد التاريخ النهائي لتسليم العطاءات. يجب تسليم نسخة أصلية من العطاء بالاضافة الى نسخة غير أصلية واحد فقط.
  6. يجب أن يرفق مع العطاء كفالة دخول عطاء وفقا للنموذج المدرج في وثائق المناقصة، وتكون قيمة كفالة دخول العطاء 3% من قيمة العطاء (مجموع اسعار البنود التي قدم لها المناقص سعراً في عرضه) والكفالة صالحة لمدة 180 يوم تقويميا من الموعد النهائي لتسليم العطاءات .
  7. العطاءات التي تصل بعد التاريخ والوقت المحددين سيتم استبعادها، وسيتم فتح العطاءات فور انتهاء الموعد المحدد بحضور ممثلي المناقصين الذين يرغبون في ذلك في العنوان المبين أدناه.

procnotices.notice_text:
Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience Program Using the Multiphase Programmatic Approach (P180127)

 

AVISO PARA MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE

 (SERVIÇO DE CONSULTORIA-CONSULTOR INDIVIDUAL)

 

PAÍS: São Tomé e Príncipe

Nome do Projeto: Programa de Preparação, Resposta e Resiliência a Emergências de Saúde Utilizando a Abordagem Programática Multifásica (P180127)

N.º do Empréstimo/ N.º do Crédito: IDA – E2280

Serviço de Consultoria Individual: Contratação do(a) Coordenador(a) para o Projeto HERR

Referência N.º 33/C/HERR/2025

 

O Governo da República Democrática de São Tomé e Príncipe (GoRDSTP), através do Ministério do Planeamento, Finanças e Economia Azul (MPFEA), recebeu um Donativo da Associação Internacional para o Desenvolvimento (IDA), para financiar os custos do Programa de preparação, resposta e resiliência a emergências de saúde e pretende aplicar parte dos recursos do donativo em pagamentos elegíveis nos termos do Contrato de um(a) Coordenador(a) para o Projeto HERR.

 

O objetivo do recrutamento é essencialmente garantir a implementação bem-sucedida do Projeto de Preparação, Resposta e Resiliência a Emergências de Saúde do STP, a fim de alcançar as metas/indicadores definidos no desenvolvimento do Projeto.

 

O objetivo deste recrutamento prende-se com os seguintes aspetos:

 

  • Assegurar que o Projeto de Preparação, Resposta e Resiliência a Emergências de Saúde de STP na sua plenitude seja mais eficiente, permitindo a monitorização regular dos recursos e responder/ultrapassar a quaisquer bloqueios e/ou desafios encontrados;

 

  • Garantir que os fundos do projeto sejam utilizados de acordo com os procedimentos do Banco Mundial;

 

  • Permitir que São Tomé e Príncipe continue a ser elegível para assistência do Banco;

 

  • Reforçar a capacidade institucional nacional para a implementação de medidas de saúde pública em conformidade com os padrões internacionais;

 

  • Promover a transferência de conhecimento e competências para técnicos nacionais, assegurando a sustentabilidade das ações após o término do projeto

 

Assim sendo, AFAP, na qualidade da Agência responsável pela parte Fiduciária e Administrativa deste Projecto, tem a honra de convidar os interessados, a formalizarem suas candidaturas num envelope fechado, em presença, correio ou por via e-mail, anexando uma Carta de Intenção dirigida ao Director-Geral da AFAP, cópia do B.I, Curriculum Vitae assinado e os comprovativos das formações e aptidões conforme declarada no Currículo.

 

Os três candidatos melhores colocados na avaliação curricular serão submetidos a entrevista.

 

O(A) consultor (a) terá as seguintes tarefas e responsabilidades:

  1. Coordenar todas as atividades relacionadas com o projeto observando as diretrizes do manual de Operações do Project (MOP);
  2. Coordenar e supervisionar a execução das atividades técnicas do projeto;
  3. Coordenar e atuar como secretário das reuniões do Comité Diretor do Projeto, composto pelos Ministros ou seus respetivos representantes das pastas do Ministério da Saúde, Economia e Finanças, assim como pelo representante da Agência Fiduciária de Administração de Projetos (AFAP); e
  4. Coordenar e liderar a Unidade de Implementação do Projeto (UIP) do Projeto de Preparação, Resposta e Resiliência a Emergências de Saúde componente de STP e supervisionar a gestão diária do projeto.

 

Duração do contrato e renovação

 

O contrato terá vigência de maio/2026 a dezembro/2026 renovável mediante desempenho considerado satisfatório. A renovação do contrato está sujeita à obtenção de uma nota acima de 80% na avaliação de desempenho e à não objeção do Banco Mundial. Os seguintes Indicadores-chave de desempenho (KPIs) serão utilizados para avaliar o desempenho:

  • Apresentar ao Banco Mundial o Plano de Trabalho Anual e o Orçamento do Projeto, conforme previsto no contrato de financiamento do projeto, antes de 31 de outubro;
  •  Preparação e apresentação de relatórios trimestrais do projeto (até 45 dias após o final do trimestre);
  • Preparar e submeter o relatório anual do Projecto, obter sua validação pelo MSD e submeter ao Banco Mundial até 1 de Março do ano seguinte.

O (a) candidato (a) a vaga de Coordenador(a) do Projeto de Preparação, Resposta e Resiliência a Emergências de Saúde deverá possuir qualificações, competências e experiências descritas abaixo:

 

  • Ser titular de um grau académico mínimo de Mestrado (ou equivalente) em Saúde Pública, Epidemiologia, Medicina, Estatística (preferencialmente aplicada à saúde), Ciências Sociais, Gestão, Administração Pública ou áreas afins relevantes;
  • Experiência profissional mínima de 10 anos em gestão de programas de saúde ou outras áreas relevantes da Saúde Pública, incluindo, preferencialmente, experiência em contextos de resposta a emergências sanitárias;
  • Experiência comprovada na implementação e/ou gestão de projetos financiados por instituições financeiras multilaterais e de desenvolvimento incluindo o Banco Mundial, agências bilaterais de desenvolvimento, e familiaridade com os respetivos procedimentos operacionais e fiduciários. Experiência de trabalho similar no sector privado será também valorizada;
  • Domínio das Tecnologias de Informação e Comunicação (TIC) na ótica de utilizador, incluindo proficiência no uso das ferramentas do Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint e Access), sendo valorizado o conhecimento de outras ferramentas de gestão de projetos e análise de dados;
  • Excelentes competências de comunicação oral e escrita em língua portuguesa, sendo a proficiência profissional em inglês e/ou francês considerada uma vantagem;
  • Elevado sentido de responsabilidade, integridade profissional, capacidade de trabalhar em equipa e sob pressão e orientação para resultados, com cumprimento rigoroso de prazos.

 

 

 

 

Chama-se a atenção dos Consultores interessados para a Secção III, parágrafos, 3.14, 3.16 e 3.17 do "Regulamento de Aquisições para Mutuários do IPF" do Banco Mundial, setembro de 2025 ("Regulamento de Aquisições"), que estabelece a política do Banco Mundial em matéria de conflito de interesses.

 

O prazo limite para o envio da candidatura é até 17h:00 (hora local) do dia 14/04/2026, conforme o endereço abaixo. As candidaturas remetidas via e-mail, devem ser enviadas para o endereço eletrónico: saúde_regional.procurement@afap.st .

 

Para ter acesso aos Termos de Referência, o interessado deverá formular o pedido por e-mail, para o endereço electrónico acima.

REPÚBLICA DE ANGOLA

MINISTÉRIO DA ADMINISTRAÇÃO DO TERRITÓRIO

PROJECTO DE FORTALECIMENTO DA GOVERNAÇÃO PARA MELHORIA DA PRESTAÇÃO DE SERVIÇOS EM ANGOLA – NJILA

Unidade de Implementação do Projecto (UIP)

 

Solicitação de Manifestação de Interesse

 

País: Angola.

Nome do Projecto: Projecto Njila.

Projecto ID N. º P178040.

Descrição do Contrato: Contratação de um (a) Especialista de Desenvolvimento Social para a URIP3

No. do Contrato: AO-MAT-534965-CS-INDV

 

O Governo de Angola assinou um acordo de empréstimo com o Banco Mundial, para a implementação do Projecto de Fortalecimento da Governança para a Melhoria da Prestação dos Serviços em Angola, cujos objectivos são: (i) Aumentar o montante e a fiabilidade das transferências fiscais para municípios seleccionados; (ii) reforçar a sua capacidade financeira e de gestão fundiária; (iii) aumentar a cobertura de identidade.

O Projecto é multissectorial, envolvendo os seguintes Departamentos Ministeriais: Ministério das Finanças, Justiça e dos Direitos Humanos, Obras Públicas, Urbanismo e Habitação, Administração Pública, Trabalho, Segurança Social e o Ministério da Administração do Território, que tem a responsabilidade de coordenar, através de uma Unidade de Implementação do Projecto (UIP).

O Projecto terá a duração de quatro (4) anos e para assegurar a sua  implementação torna-se necessário preencher o quadro de pessoal da Unidade Regional de Implementação do Projecto (URIP), com técnicos capazes de dar suporte a execução, incluindo um(a) Especialista em Desenvolvimento Social, para garantir o cumprimento e conformidade social ao nível do projecto, apoiando a coordenação na implementação das actividades relacionadas com as questões sociais durante toda a fase de implementação do Projecto NJILA.

O objectivo geral desta consultoria (os serviços) é de assumir a responsabilidade pela implementação dos instrumentos preparados no âmbito do projecto, a nível regional, nomeadamente Quadro de Gestão Ambiental e Social (QGAS), Plano de Compromissos Ambientais e Sociais (PCAS), Procedimentos de Gestão de Mão-de-Obra (PGMO), entre outros.

A duração desta contratação é de 12 meses, renováveis em função do desempenho satisfatório. Os Termos de Referência podem ser obtidos no endereço abaixo indicado.

O Projecto de Fortalecimento da Governança para a Melhoria da Prestação de Serviços em Angola, convida os candidatos “interessados” (Consultores Especialistas em Desenvolvimento Social) elegíveis a manifestarem o seu interesse em prestar os serviços. Os candidatos interessados deverão fornecer informações que demonstrem qualificações requeridas e experiência relevante para executar os serviços.

O(A) Candidato(a) deve possuir as seguintes qualificações: (I) Possuir formação superior ao nível de licenciatura em Sociologia, Antropologia, Geografia ou outras áreas afins; (II) Possuir formação ao nível de mestrado é uma vantagem; (III) Possuir um curso ou treinamento em Violência Baseada no Género é uma vantagem; (IV) pelo menos, 2 (dois) anos de experiência relevante para este posto; (V) Experiência com as Políticas de Salvaguardas do Banco Mundial e noções básicas sobre o Novo Quadro Ambiental e Social; e a legislação nacional angolana é uma vantagem; (VI) Experiência na condução e monitoria de EIAS/PGAS. Vantagem será dada a candidatos com experiência na Gestão de Mecanismos de Queixas e Reclamações; (VII) Experiência profissional comprovada de mais de 3 (três) anos na área de desenvolvimento social ou comunitário; (VIII) Experiência na implementação de planos de mitigação de riscos sociais e em avaliação de Impactos Sociais; (IX) Conhecimento dos aspectos relativos à higiene e segurança ocupacional e nas comunidades; (X) Alguma experiência com treinamento técnico e / ou capacitação tanto em nível central quanto em comunidade / local; (XI) Comprovada capacidade técnica, analítica, escrita e comunicação, bem como algum conhecimento do trabalho do Banco Mundial, incluindo procedimentos fiduciários e administrativos; (XII) Domínio na língua portuguesa é essencial, e fluência na escrita e fala em inglês é essencial.

Os candidatos deverão ter atenção ao Regulamento de Aquisições do Banco Mundial para Mutuários de Financiamentos de Projectos de Investimento de Setembro de 2025, à Secção III, parágrafos 3.14, 3.16, e 3.17 das referidas Normas, que definem a política do Banco Mundial sobre o conflito de interesse. O referido documento pode ser consultado na seguinte hiperligação:https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/products-and-services/brief/procurement-new-framework.

Os interessados deverão obter informação adicional no endereço abaixo indicado das 8H00 às 15H00. procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

CONSULTANT’S QUALIFICATIONS BASED SELECTION (CQS)

 

Name of Project

Secure, Affordable, and Sustainable Energy for Sri Lanka

Loan No/Credit No/ Grand Number

P505052

Assignment Title

Consultancy Services to prepare the specification of the Synchronous Condenser at the New Habarana Grid Substation

Procurement Plan Ref Number

.

Country of Delivery

Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka

The Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Installation of a 75 MVA synchronous condenser at New Habarana GSS and intends to apply part of the proceeds for the following consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include: (a) site assessment and data collection, including review of existing grid studies and operational data, and identification of technical;  spatial, and integration constraints; (b) evaluation of system requirements covering grid stability, reactive power and voltage control needs, future expansion scenarios, and determination of key synchronous condenser technical parameters, including excitation, flywheel sizing, short-circuit contribution, and environmental and seismic considerations; and (c) development of technical specifications and procurement support, including detailed specifications for design, auxiliaries, protection and control, SCADA integration, testing and commissioning, warranties and spares, and delivery of a structured knowledge-sharing program for National System Operator (NSO) staff. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment is attached to this REOI.

The assignment will be carried out by a multidisciplinary team of experts comprised of an Electrical Engineer / Synchronous Condenser Specialist, Mechanical Engineer (Large Rotating Equipment), Protection, Control and Automation Engineer (P&C/SCADA), and Grid Studies and Power Quality Specialist, with complementary expertise covering synchronous condenser design and performance, excitation and auxiliary systems, mechanical and vibration aspects of large rotating machines, protection and control systems for transmission substations, SCADA and communication interfaces, and power system stability and dynamic performance analysis. The assignment is expected to span 45 calendar days from the start date, with an anticipated commencement in first quarter of 2026.

The NSO now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The best qualified firm to carry out the services will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Qualifications Based Selection (CQS) method set out in the Regulations and based on the following criteria: (a) proven experience in power system studies and grid integration of synchronous condensers in high-renewable transmission networks; and (b) demonstrated experience in specification and design of synchronous condensers of similar size or larger.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, sixth edition, February 2025 (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 8:30 am to 4:00 pm.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by e-mail) by 15/04/2026

Attn: Eng. (Dr) H M Wijekoon Banda

National System Operator (Pvt) Ltd

5th Floor, Office of Power System Planning Branch

 No 50, Sir Chittampalam A. Gardiner Mw

Colombo 02

Sri Lanka

Tel: +94 112 324 842

E-mail: hmwijekoon@gmail.com, copy kushan.marambage@ceb.lk

 

__________________________________________________________________________________________

___________________________________TOR___________________________________________________

Preparation of Technical Specifications for Installation of a 75 MVA Synchronous Condenser at New Habarana Grid Substation and Support with Procurement Process

Terms of Reference

  1. Background

In line with Sri Lanka’s commitment to sustainable development, the government has set ambitious energy policy targets, aiming to achieve 70% of electricity generation from renewable energy sources by 2030 and reach carbon neutrality by 2050. Sri Lanka’s electricity demand is experiencing sustained growth driven by economic development, and tourism growth. In the meantime, the government aims to decrease dependence on imported fossil fuels and lower electricity costs by diversifying the energy mix and leveraging the country’s extensive renewable energy resources. These developments necessitate enhancements in grid stability, reliability, and operational flexibility to support both current needs and anticipated future expansions.

In July 2025, the World Bank’s Board of Directors approved the Secure, Affordable and Sustainable Energy to Sri Lanka project (SASE, P505052), which will finance critical grid investments.  SASE is the World Bank’s flagship initiative aimed at strengthening Sri Lanka’s power sector infrastructure to deliver more secure, affordable, and sustainable energy to all citizens. The project encompasses the upgrade and expansion of transmission assets, integration of renewable energy sources, and the deployment of advanced technologies to modernize the grid. Within this broader context, the installation of a 75 MVA synchronous condenser at New Habarana Grid Substation has been identified as a critical investment.

The New Habarana Grid Substation is a pivotal node in Sri Lanka’s national transmission network, strategically located to facilitate the transfer of bulk power between key regions. The synchronous condenser is intended to enhance system inertia, improve voltage regulation, and provide rapid reactive power support—functions that are vital for mitigating the volatility associated with higher penetration of renewable energy. The addition of this equipment aligns with the project’s strategic goals to ensure grid resilience, reduce vulnerability to disturbances, and facilitate the ongoing transition toward a cleaner energy mix. Furthermore, the New Habarana Grid Substation’s role as an interconnection point for multiple transmission corridors makes it a priority location for dynamic grid support measures. The synchronous condenser will enable the substation to help balance supply and demand fluctuations, support fault recovery, and meet stringent power quality standards as outlined in the project’s technical assessment.

In recognition of these challenges and opportunities, engaging a qualified consulting firm to help Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB) prepare robust technical specifications for the synchronous condenser is essential. The Consultant’s work will guarantee that the procurement process is competitive and transparent, and that the delivered solution addresses the operational, environmental, and regulatory requirements detailed in the project’s foundational documents.

  1. Objective of Work

The primary objective is to engage a consulting service to prepare comprehensive technical specifications for the installation and commissioning of a 75 MVA synchronous condenser at the New Habarana Grid Substation. The specifications should ensure robust performance, address all relevant technical, environmental, and operational considerations, clearly define contractual scope, and facilitate competitive procurement. Specifically, the Consultant is expected to:

  • Analyze the grid’s operational requirements and recommend optimal technical solutions.
  • Prepare detailed technical specifications covering design, supply, installation, testing, and commissioning of the synchronous condenser.
  • Ensure that the specifications enable interoperability, future scalability, and compliance with prevailing standards.
  1. Scope of Work

Task 1: Site Assessments and Data Collection. The Consultant will carry out the following main activities:

  • Conduct thorough site visits to New Habarana Grid Substation.
  • Collect existing single-line diagrams, grid studies, and historical operational data.
  • Identify integration points, auxiliary systems, and spatial constraints for installation.

Task 2: Evaluation of System Requirements. The Consultant will carry out the following main activities:

  • Analyse grid stability, reactive power requirements, and voltage control needs at New Habarana GSS, considering present and future network conditions, high renewable energy penetration, and planned transmission reinforcements. The list of available documents is presented in Annex 1.
  • Evaluate future expansion scenarios (to be provided by CEB), operational contingencies, and possible upgrades.
  • Carry out additional analytical work required for evaluating the technical parameters and determining the specifications of the required synchronous condenser, including the excitation system (i.e. Static/brushless excitor)  parameters suitable for Sri Lankan use case, sizing of flywheel, short time reactive power capability, short circuit contribution, special design requirements: (i.e. over voltages, Xd”(sat), Xd’(sat), losses, etc.)
  • Assess the environmental, seismic, and other factors which may influence equipment design.

Task 3: Development of Technical Specifications. The Consultant will carry out the following main activities:

  • Draft detailed technical specifications for the synchronous condenser, including:
    • Rated capacity (75 MVA), voltage, frequency, insulation class, and cooling requirements.
    • Auxiliary systems: excitation, protection, control, and monitoring equipment.
    • Mechanical structure, installation footprint, vibration and noise mitigation measures.
    • SCADA integration, remote monitoring, and data acquisition interfaces.
    • Operational modes (automatic/manual), start-up/shut-down sequences, fault handling.
    • Maintenance requirements and lifecycle support provisions.
    • Compliance with IEC, IEEE, and relevant national standards.
  • Specify testing protocols for factory acceptance, site acceptance, and commissioning.
  • Define warranty, after-sales support, and spares requirements.
  • Conduct a knowledge sharing session (online) on specification development, including the following areas. (duration: 4 days, 7 hours per day)
  1. Grid requirements and power system studies,
  2. Technical requirements, Performance guarantees, Case Studies,
  3. Testing, commissioning and maintenance.
  1. Team Composition and Qualification Requirements for the Key Experts

The Consultant’s team should be comprised of the following key experts, and they should meet the following requirements.

 

Key Expert

Qualification Requirements

Grid Studies and Power Quality Specialist

At least Master’s in power systems, electrical engineering. At least 12 years of international relevant experience in power system analysis (steady-state and dynamic) using PSS®E, PowerFactory, PSCAD or equivalent tools. Experience in development/validation of dynamic models for synchronous condensers; assessment of inertia contribution, short-circuit support, reactive power/voltage regulation, fault recovery, and stability margins; experience drafting performance test protocols for grid-code compliance. Excellent knowledge of English language.

Electrical Engineer / Synchronous Condenser Specialist

At least Master’s in electrical engineering or another relevant field. At least 12 years of relevant international experience with large synchronous machines (75 MVA or larger), including excitation systems, cooling, starting methods, auxiliaries, vibration, and insulation. Participation in at least two projects covering FAT, SAT, and commissioning of synchronous condensers or large generators repurposed as condensers. Excellent knowledge of English language.

Protection, Control and Automation Engineer (P&C/SCADA)

At least Master’s in electrical engineering, automation, or controls engineering. At least 12 years of relevant international experience in protection and control for transmission substations and large rotating machines. Experience specifying and setting generator/condense mode protections (differential, stator/rotor earth fault, negative sequence, OEL/UEL, out-of-step), AVR interfaces, and PSS interactions; SCADA/DAS integration (IEC 61850, IEC 60870-5-104, DNP3), time sync (PTP/IRIG-B), alarm/event recording, and cybersecurity considerations. Excellent knowledge of English language.

Mechanical Engineer

At least Master’s in mechanical engineering or another relevant field. At least 12 years of relevant international experience in large rotating equipment (generators/condensers, large motors, turbomachinery); bearings, lubrication, sealing, cooling, alignment, rotor dynamics and vibration diagnostics (ISO 10816/20816 or equivalent); design review of enclosures, acoustic/noise mitigation, HVAC; hydrogen safety (where relevant). Excellent knowledge of English language.

Further, the consulting firm would be responsible for determining whether further experts are required. The above is the minimum requirement.

  1. Deliverables

For transmission system level analysis or other specialized tasks, when Consultant will be using specialized software, the outputs should be submitted both in the forma of the original software utilized and PDF/excel/Word to facilitate the review.

The Forestry and Wildlife Committee of the Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources of the Republic of Kazakhstan (PROGREEN Project Implementation Group) invites contractors to submit quotations for the works described in Annex 1: Requirements for Works attached to this RFQ.

Eligible Materials, Equipment, and Services

Materials, equipment, and services to be supplied under the Contract and financed by the Bank may originate from any country, except: None.

Validity of Quotations

Quotations shall remain valid until April 14, 2025.

Price

The Contractor shall indicate the total price in the Contractor’s quotation.

The Contractor must also provide unit rates and prices for all items of the Works described in the attached Bill of Quantities. Items for which no rates or prices are entered will not be paid for by the Employer when executed and shall be deemed covered by other rates and prices in the Bill of Quantities.

Technical Proposal

The Contractor shall submit a technical proposal including a description of work methods, equipment, personnel, schedule, and any other relevant information in sufficient detail to demonstrate the adequacy of the proposal to meet the requirements and completion timeframe.

Clarifications

Any request for clarification of this RFQ may be sent in writing to:

010000, Republic of Kazakhstan, Astana,
1 Almaty Street, “Asyl-Tau” Business Center,
14th floor, office 1403.
Phone: +7 702 792 8683
E-mail: projectimplemintationgroup@gmail.com

The Employer will send copies of its response to all Contractors, including a description of the inquiry but without identifying its source.

Submission of Quotations

Quotations shall be submitted using the form provided in Annex 2.

Deadline for submission of quotations: January 28, 2025

Submission address:
010000, Republic of Kazakhstan, Astana,
1 Almaty Street, “Asyl-Tau” Business Center,
14th floor, office 1403
PROGREEN Project Implementation Unit

Murato v E.K. – Head of the Project Implementation Unit
Phone: +7 776 675 0988
Contact person: Altina Anel

Opening of Quotations

Quotations will be opened by the Employer’s representatives immediately after the submission deadline.

Evaluation of Quotations

Quotations will be evaluated for technical responsiveness.

For technically compliant quotations, total prices excluding provisional sums and contingencies, but including dayworks (where priced competitively), will be compared to determine the lowest evaluated quotation.

For evaluation and comparison purposes, quotation currencies will be converted into a single currency. The currency for comparison shall be Kazakhstani Tenge (KZT). The exchange rate source shall be the National Bank of the Republic of Kazakhstan. The exchange rate date shall be January 28, 2025.

Contract Award

The Contract will be awarded to the Contractor who:

a) offers the lowest evaluated price;
b) submits a technically responsive quotation; and
c) confirms completion of the Works within the required timeframe.

The Employer will promptly notify other Contractors of the contract award decision. Unsuccessful Contractors may request clarification of the reasons why their quotation was not successful. The Employer will respond within a reasonable time.

Fraud and Corruption

The Bank requires compliance with its Anti-Corruption Guidelines and its prevailing sanctions policies and procedures, as set forth in the World Bank Group Sanctions Framework, as specified in Annex A to the Contract Conditions.

To further this policy, the Contractor shall permit the Bank to inspect all accounts, records, and other documents relating to the RFQ and contract performance (in case of award), and to have them audited by auditors appointed by the Bank.

procnotices.notice_text:
Date: March 30, 2026

Title: MSME Competitiveness Project        

ID No. P177895

of Funding: Loan No.: IBRD 9423-MD & Credit No.: IDA 7174-MD

number: MD-CEP-485634-GO-RFQ

 

To: Potential Suppliers

 

Dear Supplier,

  1. You are hereby invited to submit a price offer for the supply of mobile scales intended for the inspection and weighing of the total mass, the permissible axle loads of cargo, and heavy-duty transport units (as per the table below)

#

Description of goods

Quantity
  1.  

Mobile weighing scale consisting of two (2) portable weighing platforms and a portable display indicator and leveling mats, designed for the inspection and weighing of the total mass, permissible axle loads of cargo of heavy-duty transport units

5 units

Information on technical specifications and required quantities is attached.

 

2. You must quote for all the items under any lot and for any lot (s) under this invitation. Price quotations will be evaluated for all the items together under each lot and each lot shall be evaluated separately and contract awarded to the firm(s) offering the lowest evaluated price for each lot or to the firm offering the lowest evaluated price for both lots. Incomplete or partial Quotes will not be considered. Alternative quotations/options are not allowed.

 

3. Your price quotation in the form attached in PDF format shall be submitted electronically. Your price quotation shall be submitted by e-mail to the following addresses:

 

E-mail for submission of the clarifications: piu@mded.gov.md

E-mail for submission of the quotations: procurementmgf@gmail.com 

Only the notification of quotation submission must be sent to piu@mded.gov.md

 

4. The deadline for receipt of your quotation (s) by the Purchaser at the electronic address indicated above is: April 16, 2026, 11:00 (local time). Late quotations will be rejected.

 

5. Your quotation in English, should be accompanied by general information about the bidder (copy of registration certificate) and adequate technical documentation and catalogue(s) and other material or pertinent information for each item quoted, including names and addresses of authorized firms or distributors, which can provide service facilities for this type of equipment in the Republic of Moldova.

 

6. Procurement of the required goods and services is carried out in accordance with the Request for Quotations (RFQ) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”).

 

7. Your quotation(s) shall be submitted as per the following instructions and in accordance with the attached Contract. The attached Terms and Conditions of Supply form an integral part of the Contract.

 

PRICES: The prices shall be quoted for delivery DDP Chisinau (MD-2001, Chisinau, Republic of Moldova, 6, Aleea Gării Street) for imported goods, per INCOTERMS, 2020. Prices can be quoted in any Bank member country currency, but no more than three currencies.

 

​​​​​​​EVALUATION OF QUOTATIONS: Quotation determined to be substantially responsive to the technical specifications will be evaluated by comparison of the total price, excluding local taxes, at destination as per para above, converting to Moldavan Leu based on the selling exchange rate offered by the National Bank of Moldova (as published by the bank on http://www.bnm.md) on the date specified in Paragraph 4 of this RFQ.

 

In evaluating the quotations, the Purchaser will determine for each quotation the evaluated price by adjusting the price quotation by making any correction for any arithmetical errors as follows:

(a) where there is a discrepancy between amounts in figures and in words, the amount in words will govern;

(b) where there is a discrepancy between the unit rate and the line-item total resulting from multiplying the unit rate by the quantity, the unit rate as quoted will govern.

(c) If a Supplier refuses to accept the correction, its quotation will be rejected.

​​​​​​​AWARD OF CONTRACT: The award will be made to the bidder offering the lowest evaluated substantially responsive quotation that meets the required technical specifications. The successful bidder will sign a Contract as per attached form of contract and terms and conditions of supply.

 

​​​​​​​VALIDITY OF THE OFFER: Your quotation(s) shall be valid for a period of forty-five (45) days from the deadline for receipt of quotation(s) indicated in Paragraph 4 of this Request for Quotation.

 

8. Further information can be obtained during office hours from 09:00 to 17:00 hours (Chisinau time) from:

Public Institution “Project Implementation Unit of the World Bank Competitiveness Enhancement Project” 180, Stefan cel Mare, office 815, MD-2004, Chisinau, Republic of Moldova

Tel: (+373 22) 296 723, e-mail: piu@mded.gov.md

 

9. Inspections and Audits

 

  1. The Supplier shall carry out all instructions of the Purchaser which comply with the applicable laws where the destination is located.
  2. The Supplier shall permit, and shall cause its Subcontractors and consultants to permit, the Bank and/or persons appointed by the Bank to inspect the Supplier’s offices and all accounts and records relating to the performance of the Contract and the submission of the bid, and to have such accounts and records audited by auditors appointed by the Bank if requested by the Bank. The Supplier’s and its Subcontractors and consultants’ attention is drawn to Clause 6. Fraud and Corruption of the Form of Contract, which provides, inter alia, that acts intended to materially impede the exercise of the Bank’s inspection and audit rights constitute a prohibited practice subject to contract termination (as well as to a determination of ineligibility pursuant to the Bank’s prevailing sanctions procedures).

 

10. A prospective bidder requiring any clarification of the Invitation to Quote shall contact the Purchaser in writing at the Purchaser’s address specified in the Paragraph 8. The Purchaser will respond in writing to any request for clarification, provided that such request is received no later than four (4) calendar days prior to the deadline for receiving of quotes.

 

11. Please confirm by e-mail the receipt of this invitation and whether you will submit the price quotation(s).

 

 

Sincerely,

     Aureliu Casian,

Executive Director

THE DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST REPUBLIC OF SRI LANKA

Ministry of Digital Economy

GovTech Sri Lanka (Private) Limited

General Procurement Notice

Project Name: Sri Lanka Digital Transformation

Practice area / sector: Digital Development

Credit No.  IDA-79530-001

Project ID No. P508317

The Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka has received financing in the amount of US$ 50 million equivalent from the World Bank toward the cost of the Sri Lanka Digital Transformation project, and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services to be procured under this project.

The project will include the following components:  

Component 1: Digital Government and Services: will invest in cross-cutting digital platforms and systems to enhance service delivery and government efficiency, promote broad-based digital adoption among citizens and public officials, and support the operationalization of empowered digital institutions. Under this component, procurements are expected to center on information systems, goods, consulting, and non-consulting services to develop and/or deploy: an online citizen and business service portal and associated mobile application (SuperApp) and digital solutions to maximize the functionality of the service portal and mobile application, including digital locker, digital authentication, and electronic signature solutions; a National Data Exchange (NDX) to serve as the technical backbone of government interoperability; government-wide collaboration and communication tools to provide a unified digital workspace for public officials across government ministries and agencies; a secure and scalable government hybrid cloud solution (GovCloud); capacity building for government digital champions to support digital transformation efforts across government entities; digital literacy trainings, citizen service desks, and information, communications, and education campaign to promote universal access to digital services; policy and operationalization support for GovTech Sri Lanka and other digital institutions.                                                                                                  

Component 2: Digital Startup Ecosystem and IT Industry Development: will support both emerging digital startups and more established, midsize IT firms to expand into new international markets and attract new customers and investments. Under this component, procurements are expected to center on consulting, and non-consulting services to: develop a comprehensive IT industry development strategy for Sri Lanka; deliver a startup acceleration and ecosystem-building program, including targeted support for women-led startups; and to provide market access support for mid-sized IT services and technology firms, through targeted export promotion initiatives and capacity building.

Component 3: Project Management, Monitoring, and Coordination: will finance project management and coordination, including procurement, financial management (FM), monitoring and evaluation (M&E), and environmental and social (E&S) risk management aspects of the project.

Procurement of contracts financed by the World Bank will be conducted through the procedures as specified in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers - September 2025 (Procurement Regulations), and is open to all eligible firms and individuals as defined in the Procurement Regulations. After project negotiations, the World Bank shall arrange the publication on its external website of the agreed initial procurement plan and all subsequent updates once it has provided a no objection.

Specific procurement notices for contracts subject to open international competitive procurement will be announced, as they become available on the World Bank’s external website and https://promise.lk/ and https://govtech.lk/ websites and “Daily News” and “Sunday Observer” newspapers.

Interested eligible firms and individuals who would wish to be considered for the provision of goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services for the above-mentioned project, or those requiring additional information, should contact the Borrower at the address below:

  1. The Government of Kenya (GoK) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Health Emergency Preparedness Response and Resilience Project (HEPRR) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.
  2. This Addendum is issued pursuant to the provisions of the World Bank “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” First Published July 2016 and Revised Fourth Edition, November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), to extend the deadline for submission of Expressions of Interest, to allow interested consultants additional time to prepare and submit responsive EOIs.

CONSULTING SERVICES FOR PREPARATION OF PRELIMINARY ENGINEERING DESIGNS, EMPLOYER REQUIREMENTS AND CONSTRUCTION SUPERVISION, AND GOOD MANUFACTURING PRACTICE COMPLIANCE CERTIFICATION FOR ESTABLISHMENT OF A HUMAN VACCINES AND BIOLOGICALS FILL–FINISH MANUFACTURING FACILITY

1. The Government of Kenya (GoK) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Health Emergency Preparedness Response and Resilience  (HEPRR) Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

2. The consulting services (“the Services”) includes consulting services for Preparation of Preliminary Engineering Designs, Employer Requirements and Construction Supervision, and Good Manufacturing Practice Compliance Certification for Establishment of a Human Vaccines and Biologicals Fill–Finish Manufacturing Facility. The duration of the assignment will be Thirty-Six (36) Months from the contract commencement date.

3. The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be found at the following Kenya Biovax Institute Limited’s website: www.biovax.go.ke.

4. The Kenya Biovax Institute Limited now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required  qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

4.1 Core business and years in business

The consulting firm shall be legally registered/incorporated as a consulting entity and shall have its core business providing expertise in project management, preparation of preliminary designs, employers requirements, construction supervision, GMP compliance certification support and technology transfer projects oversight for pharmaceutical/biopharmaceutical/human vaccines and biologicals manufacturing companies, for a minimum period of ten (10) years.

4.2  Relevant experience:

 The consulting firm shall demonstrate having successfully executed, completed and supported GMP compliance certification of at least one (1) assignment of similar nature, scope, scale, and complexity within the last ten (10) years.

Details of similar assignments shall be provided in the expression of interest, including the Client’s name and address, scope of services, contract value, period of execution, and the consultant’s role.

4.3Technical and managerial capability of the firm:

The consulting firm shall demonstrate adequate technical capacity and managerial capability to undertake this assignment, supported by submitted company profiles, organizational structures, and availability of suitably qualified experts.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

5. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” First Published July 2016 and Revised Fourth Edition, November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

6. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

7. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations.

8. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 0900 to 1700 hours East African Time (EAT) from Monday to Friday excluding lunch hour (1300 to 1400hours (EAT) and public holidays.

9. Expressions of Interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below In person or  by mail or email and be clearly marked “Expression of Interest Preparation of Preliminary Engineering Designs, Employer Requirements and Construction Supervision, and Good Manufacturing Practice Compliance Certification for Establishment of a Human Vaccines and Biologicals Fill–Finish Manufacturing Facility” by 7th April 2026 at 1000 hours East African Time.

Empréstimo Nº /Crédito Nº /Doação N°: IBRD 9601-BR

Processo Sigadoc: SEDUC-PRO-2026/10799

Número do Step: BR-SEDUC-MT-454716-NC-RFB

Emitida em: 27/03/2026

 

 

O Governo do Estado de Mato Grosso recebeu financiamento do Banco Mundial para cobrir os custos do Projeto Aprendizado Digital, Inclusivo e Sustentável de Mato Grosso (PADIS-MT), e pretende destinar parte dos recursos a pagamentos no âmbito da Contratação de empresa especializada na prestação de serviços como Agência de Verificação Externa - AVE, para verificação de metas, objetivos e resultados dos projetos “Acompanhamento Personalizado da Aprendizagem - APA” (CBD 1); “Sistema de Alerta Preventivo ao Abandono e Evasão Escolar - SAPAEe” (CBD 2) e “Programa Estadual de Prevenção da Violência no Ambiente Escolar- PPV” (CBD 6.

 

A Secretaria de Estado de Educação-MT  convida os licitantes elegíveis a apresentar suas Ofertas lacradas para Contratação de empresa especializada na prestação de serviços como Agência de Verificação Externa - AVE, para verificação de metas, objetivos e resultados dos projetos “Acompanhamento Personalizado da Aprendizagem - APA” (CBD 1); “Sistema de Alerta Preventivo ao Abandono e Evasão Escolar - SAPAEe” (CBD 2) e “Programa Estadual de Prevenção da Violência no Ambiente Escolar- PPV” (CBD 6.

 

 A licitação será organizada por meio de licitação pública internacional, usando o método de Solicitação de Ofertas (SDO), conforme especificado no “Regulamento de Aquisições para os Mutuários de Operações de IPF” do Banco Mundial, de novembro de 2020- 4ª edição e estarão abertas a todos os Licitantes elegíveis, conforme definido no Regulamento de Aquisições.

 

Os Licitantes elegíveis interessados poderão obter mais informações junto à Comissão Especial de Licitações, e-mail: cel.padis@edu.mt.gov.br  e examinar o Edital de Licitação durante o horário de expediente das 08h00 às 18h00 horário de Mato Grosso no endereço abaixo [1].

O Edital de Licitação em Português-Brasileiro poderá ser adquirido pelos Licitantes interessados mediante o envio de um pedido por escrito para o e-mail cel.padis@edu.mt.gov.br. 

 

As Ofertas deverão ser entregues no endereço abaixo até  12/05/2026 e 18hr00 min. O envio de Ofertas por meios eletrônicos NÃO SERÁ permitido. As Ofertas recebidas com atraso serão rejeitadas.  As Ofertas serão abertas publicamente na presença dos representantes designados dos Licitantes e de qualquer pessoa que desejar comparecer no endereço abaixo: SEDUC/SAAS/SUAC/CEL, Rua Engenheiro Edgar Prado Arze, Quadra 01, Lote 05, Setor A - Centro Político Administrativo, Cuiabá - Mato Grosso, Cep 78049-906 – Brasil,  em 12/05/2026 e 18hs00min.

Todas as Ofertas deverão ser acompanhadas de uma Garantia da Oferta, no valor de 3% do total da oferta.

Convém atentar para o Regulamento de Aquisições, que exige do Mutuário a divulgação de informações sobre a propriedade beneficiária do Licitante vencedor, como parte do Aviso de Adjudicação do Contrato, conforme o Formulário de Divulgação de Propriedade Beneficiária previsto no Edital de Licitação.

O(s) endereço(s) referido(s) acima são o meio pelo qual terão acesso as demais condições de participação  bem como a Especificação Técnica .

E-mail: cel.padis@edu.mt.gov.br.

Consulting Services for Preparation of a Resettlement Plan for Saint Paul 2 Hydropower Project Early Construction Works (REVISED )

Project ID No.: P513900

Reference No.: LR-LEC-539959-CS-CQS

Closing Date: April 13, 2026

Background

The Liberia Electricity Corporation (LEC) has secured financing from the World Bank under the Saint Paul 2 Hydropower Project. Part of the proceeds will be applied to consulting services for the preparation of a Resettlement Plan (RP) for Phase 1 Early Construction Works.

This assignment covers one of the required Environmental and Social (E&S) instruments for Phase 1, specifically the RP. The consultant will prepare the RP, including baseline studies, census and asset valuation, inventory of losses, socioeconomic surveys, and stakeholder consultations (with special attention to vulnerable groups). The RP will outline housing, asset restoration, resettlement sites, livelihood programs, and implementation timelines.

The objectives are to:

  • Describe early construction works and anticipated land acquisition impacts.
  • Document alternatives considered and how resettlement impacts were minimized.
  • Identify risks and impacts of land acquisition.
  • Propose mitigation measures consistent with the World Bank’s Environmental and Social Framework (ESF).
  • Prepare and disclose the final RP, approved by LEC-PIU, EPA, World Bank, and affected communities.
  • Implement the RP once Phase 1 effectiveness is reached, including compensation payments.

The consulting services will be contracted by LEC and report to the RESPITE PIU E&S Deputy Manager. Deliverables will be submitted electronically to the RESPITE PIU E&S Manager and Project Director. The engagement duration is six months.

The duration of the engagement will be 6 months.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the following link: https://lecliberia.com/wp-content/uploads/20260326_ToR_for_SP2_EW_RAP-_SH-wdh-CLEAN.docx

The Liberia Electricity Corporation (LEC) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

Core business and years in business: 

The firm shall be registered/ incorporated as a consulting firm with core business in the field of the assignment.

Qualification and Experience of the Firm: 

  1. The firm selected to undertake this assignment must have significant experience designing and implementing resettlement Projects, including in West Africa. Preferably, the Consultant would have both road-expansion and hydropower related experience, with at least one assignment associated with a World Bank funded project prepared in accordance with ESF requirements.
  2. The required firm should also have demonstrated experience with the design and implementation of resettlement and livelihoods restoration programs in the region, preferably within Liberia and hydropower related.
  3. The Consultant shall identify and partner, with a local EPA- certified firm as is required by the Liberia EPA to carry out the scope of work

Technical and Managerial Capability of the Firm

  1. Proven project management structure with clear roles and reporting lines.
  2. Multidisciplinary team (resettlement, social, survey, livelihood, GIS) with relevant expertise.
  3. Ability to partner effectively with Liberia EPA-certified local firms.
  4. Established quality assurance and compliance systems aligned with World Bank ESF.
  5. Strong stakeholder engagement and grievance redress mechanisms.
  6. Capacity for data collection, asset valuation, and secure database management.
  7. Demonstrated ability to deliver assignments on time and within budget.

Note: Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (Seventh Edition, September 2025), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract.

A consulting firm will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualifications-based Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 0900 to 1600 hours GMT.
