REPÚBLICA DE ANGOLA

MINISTÉRIO DA ADMINISTRAÇÃO DO TERRITÓRIO

PROJECTO DE FORTALECIMENTO DA GOVERNAÇÃO PARA MELHORIA DA PRESTAÇÃO DE SERVIÇOS EM ANGOLA – NJILA

Unidade de Implementação do Projecto (UIP)

 

Solicitação de Manifestação de Interesse

 

País: Angola.

Nome do Projecto: Projecto Njila.

Projecto ID N. º P178040.

Descrição do Contrato: Contratação de um(a) Especialista Ambiental para a URIP2

No. do Contrato: AO-MAT-534972-CS-INDV

O Governo de Angola assinou um acordo de empréstimo com o Banco Mundial, para a implementação do Projecto de Fortalecimento da Governança para a Melhoria da Prestação dos Serviços em Angola, cujos objectivos são: (i) Aumentar o montante e a fiabilidade das transferências fiscais para municípios seleccionados; (ii) reforçar a sua capacidade financeira e de gestão fundiária; (iii) aumentar a cobertura de identidade.

O Projecto é multissectorial, envolvendo os seguintes Departamentos Ministeriais: Ministério das Finanças, Justiça e dos Direitos Humanos, Obras Públicas, Urbanismo e Habitação, Administração Pública, Trabalho, Segurança Social e o Ministério da Administração do Território, que tem a responsabilidade de coordenar, através de uma Unidade de Implementação do Projecto (UIP).

O Projecto terá a duração de quatro (4) anos e para assegurar a sua  implementação torna-se necessário preencher o quadro de pessoal da Unidade Regional de Implementação do Projecto (URIP), com técnicos capazes de dar suporte a execução, incluindo um(a) Especialista Ambiental, para garantir o cumprimento e conformidade ambiental ao nível das Unidades Regionais de Implementação do Projecto, apoiando a coordenação na implementação do das actividades relacionadas com as questões ambientais durante toda a fase de implementação. Esta contratação terá como principal função apoiar a Coordenação na garantia do cumprimento dos requisitos legais nacionais e os requisitos ambientais do BM, de acordo com o Quadro Ambiental e Social (QAS).

O objectivo geral desta consultoria (os serviços) é de assumir a responsabilidade pela implementação dos instrumentos preparados no âmbito do projecto, a nível regional, nomeadamente Quadro de Gestão Ambiental e Social (QGAS), Plano de Compromissos Ambientais e Sociais (PCAS), Procedimentos de Gestão de Mão-de-Obra (PGMO), entre outros.

A duração desta contratação é de 12 meses, renováveis em função do desempenho satisfatório. Os Termos de Referência podem ser obtidos no endereço abaixo indicado.

O Projecto de Fortalecimento da Governança para a Melhoria da Prestação de Serviços em Angola, convida os candidatos “interessados” (Consultores Especialistas Ambientais) elegíveis a manifestarem o seu interesse em prestar os serviços. Os candidatos interessados deverão fornecer informações que demonstrem qualificações requeridas e experiência relevante para executar os serviços.

O(A) Candidato(a) deve possuir as seguintes qualificações: (I) Licenciatura em Gestão Ambientais, Engenharia Ambiental, Ciências Naturais, Biologia ou em áreas afins; (II) Mínimo 2 (dois) anos de experiência relevante para esta posição; (III) Experiência na aplicação das Políticas de Salvaguardas do Banco Mundial, com o Quadro Ambiental e Social do Banco Mundial e ainda com os Padrões de Desempenho do IFC; bem como com a legislação ambiental nacional angolana aplicável; (IV) Conhecimento dos regulamentos/directivas e operações pertinentes das organizações multilaterais de desenvolvimento e das agências de execução. Mínimo de 2 anos de experiência em organizações internacionais; (V) Experiência na elaboração e monitoria de EAS/PGAS; (VI) Formação e experiência em Saúde e Segurança Ocupacional (SSO); (VII) Capacidade comprovada em trabalhar com várias partes interessadas, incluindo entidades governamentais, organizações da sociedade civil (OSCs), comunidades locais e sector privado; (VIII) Comprovada capacidade técnica, analítica, escrita e comunicação, bem como algum conhecimento do trabalho do Banco Mundial; (IX) Domínio das ferramentas informáticas, especificamente o MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint); (X) Domínio da Língua Portuguesa e inglesa.

Os candidatos deverão ter atenção ao Regulamento de Aquisições do Banco Mundial para Mutuários de Financiamentos de Projectos de Investimento de Setembro de 2025, à Secção III, parágrafos 3.14, 3.16, e 3.17 das referidas Normas, que definem a política do Banco Mundial sobre o conflito de interesse. O referido documento pode ser consultado na seguinte hiperligação:https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/products-and-services/brief/procurement-new-framework.

Os interessados deverão obter informação adicional no endereço abaixo indicado das 8H00 às 15H00. As manifestações de interesse (Currículo, cópia dos certificados de habilitações académicas e outras informações pertinentes) deverão ser entregues até o dia 10 de Abril de 2026, apenas os Consultores qualificados na etapa de avaliação curricular serão contactados para as entrevistas.

Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD)
Request for Expression of Interest
(Consulting Services – Firms Selection)
 Country: IGAD Secretariat
Name of project: Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project
Project No.:  P176181
Grant No.:  IDA-E1670

 Assignment Title: Development of Regional Guidelines for Infrastructure Sharing, Co-location, Data Hosting and Cloud Market for IGAD Member States

Reference/Contract No.: DJ-IGAD-518883-CS-CQS

The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.
The consulting services (“the Services”) include conducting the development of a harmonised regional approach for (i) connectivity infrastructure sharing and co-location, and (ii) data hosting and cloud market across IGAD Member States for IGAD Member States.The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) and Scope of Work for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://igad.int/consultancies or can be obtained at the address given below.
The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria:
The firm selected will need to demonstrate:

Extensive experience in supporting regional and or digital policies and regulations, with experience advising on various ICT policies, especially on data governance, infrastructure sharing and co-location.
Extensive experience in conducting cloud needs assessments and developing cloud strategies.
Extensive experience in providing advisory and consultancy services on data infrastructure, data markets and data governance.
A demonstrated track record of completing similar assignments, with a focus on relevance and recent experience. This includes legal reviews, the review of national/regional data governance, infrastructure sharing and co-location policies/strategies.
Prior experience in implementing national digital accessibility standards.
Prior experience of working closely with the public sector, private sector and other relevant stakeholders, especially in data governance, infrastructure sharing, co-location and integration.
Demonstrated familiarity with the Horn of Africa context.
Availability of the Key Experts indicated in the ToRs.
Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” First Published July 2016 and revised Fifth Edition September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.
Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.
A Consulting firm will be selected in accordance with the Quality And Cost-Based Selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations.
Further information can be obtained at the address below during the following office hours 0900 and 1600 hours from Monday to Friday excluding lunch hour (1300 to 1400hours East African Time (EAT) and public holidays.
Expression of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below by 20/April /2026 at 1100hours EAT using one of the following modalities: (i) deposit in the IGAD Office in the address below or (ii) send by e-mail to:  procurement@igad.int with copy to hassan.salah@igad.int and quote the Assignment title and Contract No (Consultancy for the Development of Regional Guidelines for Infrastructure Sharing, Co-location, Data Hosting and Cloud Market for IGAD Member States– Reference/Contract No.: DJ-IGAD-518883-CS-CQS) in the subject row. For expressions of interest that will be deposited at IGAD Office in Djibouti the packages should be clearly marked with assignment title and reference/contract No. as mentioned above.

procnotices.bid_description: Independent verification Consultant
procnotices.contact_address:
Department of Planning
Ministry of Education and Sports

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

 

Country:       Lao People’s Democratic Republic

Project:         Global Partnership for Education III Project: Learning and Equity Acceleration Project (LEAP), Credit No.: 6854-LA

Sector:          Education

Description: Consulting Services (Individual Consultant) to verify the Performance-Based Conditions (PBC) of the Global Partnership for Education III - Learning and Equity Acceleration Project (GPE III - LEAP)

 

Background

The Lao PDR GPE III - LEAP is a national project led by MoES, with financial support from the International Development Association (IDA), the World Bank, and the GPE. Approved on 18 March 2021 and effective from 30 August 2021, the project aims to improve learning outcomes in primary grades across target districts, while strengthening teacher performance and institutional capacity. Anchored in the vision of reducing learning poverty and promoting greater equity and accountability, the project operates through integrated support to children, teachers, and local institutions and represents a strategic commitment to inclusive, data-driven education reform in Lao PDR. The GPE grant will close on May 31, 2027, while the World Bank financing part will close on 31 May 2029.

The Ministry of Education and Sports (MoES) in Lao PDR is recruiting an experienced consultant to verify the PBC of the GPEIII:LEAP Project, to be under the Education Coordination Unit (ECU), Department of Planning.

Objectives of the assignment:

  • Independently verify achievement of each PBC against the agreed verification protocol.
  • Assess data quality (accuracy, completeness, timeliness), traceability, and controls.
  • Verify adherence to agreed procedures for measurement, reporting, and validation.
  • Provide an objective verification report to the Client and the World Bank, with clear conclusions on PBC achievement and any qualifications.

Scope of work:

The specific scope of work under each PBC is the following:

  1. Verification of PBC 1:
  • Confirm the number of districts that are compliant with the approved teacher allocation protocols. 
  • Review district implementation records through MoES-LESMIS  and conduct on-site visits   to verify compliance.
  • Confirm the districts that are compliant with teacher allocation up to 10 districts have 40 percent of public primary schools in the district with enough teachers per criteria defined in the MoES guidelines No. 8986
  1. Verification of PBC 2:
  • Verify that LESMIS platform is operational with technical architecture and API capabilities to connect to all MoES databases including: EMIS, TEMIS, PEMIS, TMIS, TVET-MIS, LUMIS, School Meal App, HEMIS, FQS, SDP, and other relevant systems;
  • Assess current integration, infrastructure, sustainability, data accuracy, and completeness, ensuring compliance with national and international standards;
  • Verify the operational status of the LESMIS platform and its dashboards, ensuring user-friendliness and accessibility for various stakeholders with reliability;
  • Verify that LESMIS data, dashboards, or visualizations were used to inform the Joint Sector Review Mission process;
  • Confirm LESMIS content was referenced or utilized during ESWG technical meetings and document its contributions to discussions and findings;
  • Review training records, attendance lists, and geographic coverage across provinces and districts including training materials, training courses and assessment results;
  • Review LESMIS technical specifications and integration status reports; data integration protocols and API documentation; system hosting and infrastructure documentation; user manuals and training materials; JSRM/ESWG meeting documentation; Annual Sector Report(s); capacity-building activity reports; metadata documentation; automated reports and dashboards; and coordination meeting records with MoES departments.
  1. Verification of PBC 3:
  • Confirm that the average score received in the classroom observation tool by teachers in priority districts that received updated training on the new Grade 1-3 curriculum meets the 3.5 points average in a sample of 40 priority districts. 
  • Review classroom observation data and conduct site visits where necessary to verify the accuracy and consistency of the scores collected, and interview school principals, teachers and COT observers.

Deliverables:

  1. Inception Report: scope, sampling, instruments, schedule, and team (within 2 weeks of contract signing). 
  2. Draft Verification Reports: separate reports for each PBC, presenting findings and evidence, tests performed, and preliminary conclusions .
  3. Final Verification Report: conclusion on achievement of each DLI/DLR; qualifications; recommended corrective actions; annexed evidence matrices.
  4. Data and evidence annexes: checklists, sample frames, test results, field notes, photos (as applicable), and reproducible calculation files.

All reports to be submitted in soft and hard copy and soft copy of data analysis shall be submitted in Lao and English.

 

Qualifications and Experience

  • Education:
    • Advanced degree (Master's or higher) in monitoring and evaluation, statistics, audit, public policy, or relevant sector expertise aligned with Program-Based Conditions (PBCs)
  • Professional Experience:
    • Minimum 10 years of progressive professional experience in monitoring and evaluation, results verification, or performance assessment
    • Demonstrated experience conducting data quality assessments and results verification, preferably in development or public sector contexts
    • At least 3 years of hands-on experience with database management, management information systems (MIS), or data analytics tools
    • Proven expertise in at least one sector relevant to the PBCs (e.g., education, information and communication technology, human resource management, or other applicable sectors)
    • Experience conducting field verification and physical site inspections is highly desirable
  • Technical Skills:
    • Strong analytical skills with ability to assess data quality, verify results against established indicators, and identify data integrity issues
    • Proficiency in statistical software and data visualization tools
    • Familiarity with public sector monitoring frameworks and performance-based financing mechanisms
    • Excellent report writing and presentation skills
  • Independence and Ethics:
    • Must have no conflict of interest with implementing entities involved in the assignment
    • Required to disclose any prior consulting engagements or relationships with entities subject to verification
    • Must comply with relevant professional independence standards and ethical guidelines
    • Commitment to maintaining objectivity and impartiality throughout the assignment

 

Duration of Assignment:
The verification process is expected to commence within 2 weeks of contract signing and will take place between May and July 2026.

The attention of interested Consultant is drawn to paragraph 1.9 of the World Bank’s Guidelines: Selection and Employment of Consultants under IBRD Loans and IDA Credits & Grants by World Bank Borrowers, January 2011 (“Consultant Guidelines”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. The Consultant will be selected based on Individual Consultants selection method set out in the Consultant Guidelines.

 

Interested eligible candidates in this position may obtain further information and the detailed TOR from the Ministry of Education and Sports, Education Coordination Unit (ECU) at the address below during office hours 08:00 to 16:00 hours or by e-mail. Please submit CVs and a letter of interest by 25 March - 10 April 2026 to the address below. Only short listed individual candidates will be contacted for an interview.

 

To:       Ministry of Education and Sports

            Lane Xang Avenue, P.O Box 67, Vientiane, Lao PDR

 

Attn:     Mr. Anoupheng Keovongsaື

procnotices.contact_organization: Palestinian Energy and Natural Resources Authority
procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Country: West Bank and Gaza

Project Name: Phase 3 Advancing Sustainability in Performance, Infrastructure, and Reliability of the Energy Sector in the West Bank and Gaza

Grant No.: P507260

Assignment Title: Sector-Wide Cybersecurity, Business Continuity, Framework & Policy Development

Reference No.: GZ-PENRA-530256-CS-QCBS

The Palestine Liberation Organization has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Phase 3 Advancing Sustainability in Performance, Infrastructure, and Reliability of the Energy Sector in the West Bank and Gaza (ASPIRE III) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include consultancy service for Sector-Wide Cybersecurity, Business Continuity, Framework & Policy Development. The expected implementation period is six (6) months.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained from the address and/or the electronic websites given below:

Attention: Procurement Officer

Al Masayef. - PENRA Building/4th floor

City: Ramallah

Telephone: +9722 2984752, or +970 2 2984752

Facsimile number: +9722 2984753 or +970 2 2984753

Electronic mail address: procurement@menr.org 

Higher Council for Public Procurement Policies’ electronic website: https://www.shiraa.gov.ps

The Palestinian Energy & Natural Resources Authority now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

1. Relevant Sector Experience

The Firm must have demonstrated experience delivering:

  • Cybersecurity frameworks and governance models
  • OT/ICS cybersecurity programs and assessments (IEC 62443 aligned)
  • BCM/DR frameworks and crisis management structures
  • Policy development and harmonization across multiple entities
  • Sector-wide or national-level cybersecurity initiatives

Minimum Requirement:

At least two (2) similar assignments in the utility, energy, critical infrastructure, or public-sector domain within the past seven years.

2. OT/ICS (IEC 62443) Expertise

The Firm must have proven experience with:

  • OT governance and lifecycle management
  • ICS/SCADA assessments, substations, PLC/RTU, historian systems
  • Zones & conduits architecture (IEC 62443-3-2)
  • OT risk assessment methodologies
  • OT-specific policy development

Minimum Requirement:

At least one major project involving IEC 62443 implementation or OT/ICS cybersecurity.

3. Information Security Framework Expertise

The Firm must demonstrate proficiency in developing and aligning frameworks with:

  • NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF)
  • ISO/IEC 27001:2022
  • ISO 22301 (BCM/DR)
  • SIEM/SOAR governance and SOC operations

Requirement:
Ability to harmonize multiple standards into a unified sector-wide approach.

4. Policy and Governance Development Capability

The Firm must demonstrate capacity to develop:

  • Comprehensive cybersecurity and SOC policies
  • OT/ICS-specific policy suites
  • BCM/DR governance policies
  • Sector-wide governance models and RACI matrices

Requirement:
Evidence of high-quality, bilingual (Arabic and English) policy outputs.

5. Regional and Institutional Knowledge

Experience working with:

  • Utilities or energy sectors in the Middle East region
  • Governmental, regulatory, or donor-funded institutions
  • Multi-stakeholder or cross-entity coordination environments

Advantage (Preferred, not mandatory):

Demonstrated familiarity with Palestinian sector dynamics.

6. Multidisciplinary Team Capacity

The Firm must be able to deploy a team with combined expertise in:

  • Cybersecurity governance
  • OT/ICS security
  • BCM/DR
  • SOC architecture and SIEM/SOAR
  • Policy drafting and documentation
  • Project management and stakeholder engagement

Requirement:
Ability to support a 6-month assignment with dedicated resources.

7. Quality Assurance & Methodology

The Firm must demonstrate:

  • Documented internal QA/QC processes

 8. Clear methodology for reviews, version control, and stakeholder alignment

  • Ability to ensure consistency across large, multi-document deliverable packages

 9. Financial and Administrative Capacity

The Firm must demonstrate the administrative capability and financial stability needed to manage a multi-entity project of this scale.

Requirement:
Audited financial statements for at least two years.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated February 2025, sixth edition (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 9:00 a.m.-2:00 p.m. (Palestine local time).

Expressions of interest must be delivered either in a written form (by courier/in person) or electronically (by email; signed, initialed, stamped, and accompanied by power of attorney to sign) to the address/email below by 12:00 p.m. (Ramallah Local Time, GMT +3) on 06/04/2026.

procnotices.contact_address: Complexo Administrativo Clássicos de Talatona, Rua do MAT, Luanda, MAT 5º Andar
procnotices.notice_text:
REPUBLIC OF ANGOLA

TERRITORIAL ADMINISTRATION MINISTRY

ANGOLA STRENGTHENING GOVERNANCE FOR ENHANCED DELIVERY PROJECT (NJILA)

 

PROJECT IMPLEMENTATION UNIT

 

Project ID N. º P178040

Request for Bids Goods

Contract Title:  Supply and installation of Computer Equipment and technological infrastructures in the 58 Municipal Administrations (Including training of technicians)

RFB Reference No.: 02/C2/G/ PROFOGMEPS/24

  1. The GoA has signed a loan agreement with the World Bank for the implementation of the Strengthening Governance to Improve Service Delivery Project, the objectives of which are: (i) to increase the amount and reliability of fiscal transfers to selected municipalities; (ii) to strengthen their financial and land management capacity; (iii) to increase identity coverage. The project is multi-sectoral, involving the following Ministerial Departments: Ministry of Finance, Justice and Human Rights, Public Works, Urban Planning and Housing, Public Administration, Labour, Social Security and the Territorial Administration, which is responsible for coordination through a Project Implementation Unit (PIU) and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contracts for Supply and installation of Computer Equipment and technological infrastructures in the 58 Municipal Administrations (Including training of technicians): For this contract, the Borrower shall process the payments using the Direct Payment disbursement method, as defined in the World Bank’s Disbursement Guidelines for Investment Project Financing..
  2. The Angola Strengthening Governance for Enhanced Delivery Project now invites sealed Bids from eligible Bidders for: Supply and Installation of Computer Equipment and Technological Infrastructures in the 58 Municipal Administrations (Including Training of Technicians).

      The procurement is structured in four (5) Lots:

  • Lot 1 – Computer Equipment for Class A Municipalities;
  • Lot 2 – Computer Equipment for Class B Municipalities;
  • Lot 3 – Equipment to Support the Delimitation of Municipalities;
  • Lot 4 – Computer Equipment for Class C Municipalities;
  • Lot 5 - End Users Devices for Municipalities (MINFIN).

The scope includes supply, delivery, installation, configuration, testing, commissioning, training, warranty and after-sales service.

Final Destination (Project Sites): Luanda, Uíge, Cuanza Sul, Benguela, Huambo, Bié, Huíla and Cunene.

Delivery and installation period: As specified in the Bidding Document.

3. Bidding will be conducted through Open International Competitive Procurement using a Request for Bids (RFB) method and is open to all eligible Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

The procurement will follow a Single-Stage, Two-Envelope procedure.

4.Technical Evaluation

The Technical Part of the Bid shall be evaluated separately for each lot using the criteria and weightings indicated in the table below. Lots 1, 2 and 4 shall be evaluated using the same criteria and respective weightings, while Lots 3 and 5 shall be evaluated using specific weightings reflecting their respective complexity and scope.
